reference_sql:
SELECT pr.promo_code, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = ol.promo_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01'
GROUP BY pr.promo_code
alternatives: SELECT pr.promo_code, COUNT(ol.order_line_id) AS n_lines FROM promotions pr JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.promo_id = pr.promo_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-02-01' AND DATE '2025-03-31' GROUP BY pr.promo_code

WITH per_promo AS (SELECT ol.promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01' AND ol.promo_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ol.promo_id) SELECT pr.promo_code, pp.n_lines FROM per_promo pp JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = pp.promo_id

other_way.sql: WITH per_promo AS (SELECT ol.promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01' AND ol.promo_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ol.promo_id) SELECT pr.promo_code, pp.n_lines FROM per_promo pp JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = pp.promo_id
other_way.tradeoff: Counting the lines per promo_id in a CTE before joining promotions keeps that join tiny, but needs one more step.

solver.query:
SELECT pr.promo_code, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
FROM order_lines l
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = l.promo_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY pr.promo_code
